files.lesson.md: --- order: 10 unit: using node: AC9M8A03 n1 uses: [AC9M7N07 n2] # a falling battery has a negative rate assumes: [AC9M8A02 n1, AC9M8A02 n3] # its Prior Knowledge; lines from rules are taught earlier in the course and solving with graphs in Solving equations with graphs (n2); inequalities are class work title: Rules from real situations summary: Many real costs and amounts are a starting amount plus a rate. The starting amount is c and the rate is m, so the rule is y = mx + c. language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Taxi fares, phone plans, gym memberships and a phone battery running down: what do they have in common?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8138 url: http://127.0.0.1:8138/index.html readySelector: "#sl-m" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: graph.yml#explain-pic, caption: "A taxi: 4 dollars to get in (where the line starts) and 2 dollars per km (up 2 for each km). $T = 2d + 4$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@graph.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "The starting amount is c; the rate is m" say: "The starting amount is c, and the rate is m." clip: - caption: { text: "A taxi costs 4 dollars to get in: that is c.", say: "A taxi costs four dollars to get in, before you go anywhere: that is c." } - click: Make c bigger - click: Make c bigger - click: Make c bigger - click: Make c bigger - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "Then 2 dollars for each km: the rate, m.", say: "Then two dollars for each kilometre: that is the rate, m." } - click: Make m bigger - click: Make m bigger - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "Together: T = 2d + 4. Starts at 4, up 2 for each km.", say: "Together, T equals two d plus four: start at four, up two per kilometre." } - expect: { selector: "#legend", contains: "T = 2d + 4" } - wait: 1200 connection: taxi-fare --- So far the rules had $x$ and $y$. Real situations have their own letters: $T$ for a total cost, $d$ for a distance, $h$ for hours. ## Predict: a taxi fare ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a rule before fitting the line shows whether students can tell the one-off amount from the rate in words." check: type: predict q: "The meter shows what this taxi charges. Which rule gives the fare $T$ for a trip of $d$ km?" options: ["$T = 2d + 4$", "$T = 4d + 2$", "$T = 6d$", "$T = 2d$"] actual: "T = 2d + 4. The 4 dollars is paid once, before you travel: it is where the line starts (c). The 2 dollars is paid for each km: it is the rate (m)." ``` Think about a trip of 0 km, then 1 km, then 2 km. What does each one cost? ## Run: fit the fares ```step stage: run insight: "Fitting a line through real fares makes c and m mean something: c is the fare for 0 km, m is the extra for each km." try: { playground: board, starter: "graph.yml#run", height: 680 } check: { type: board, text: "Set $m$ and $c$ so the line goes through all three fares.", when: "P on y = mx + c and Q on y = mx + c and R on y = mx + c" } ``` The graph works the same way as before: $m$ is how much the line goes up for each step right, and $c$ is where it starts. The points are three fares: 6 dollars for 1 km, 10 dollars for 3 km and 14 dollars for 5 km. (The fares are made up for the task.) Set $m$ and $c$ so the line passes through all three. Was your rule right? ## Investigate: from words to a rule ```step stage: investigate insight: "In words, the starting amount is the value when nothing has happened yet (c); the rate is 'per', 'each' or 'every' (m)." tasks: - picture: { ref: graph.yml#explain-pic, caption: "The taxi: starts at 4 (the fee), up 2 for each km (the rate)." } check: type: answer q: "A gym charges a 30 dollar joining fee and 15 dollars a week. Write a rule for the total cost $T$ after $w$ weeks." answer: "15w + 30" feedback: - ["30w + 15", "That charges 30 each week. Which amount is paid only once, at the start?"] - ["15w", "You have the weekly rate. What about the joining fee?"] - ["45w", "The joining fee is paid once, not every week. Keep it separate."] explain: "T = 15w + 30: 30 dollars once (c), then 15 dollars for each week (m)." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#zoe" text: "Zoe writes a rule for a taxi fare. Click the line where her reasoning goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: m-c-swap explain: "Line 2: m is the rate, the amount for each km, which is 3. It does not matter which number comes first in the question. The rule is T = 3d + 5." - check: type: question q: "A phone plan costs $T = 5g + 20$ dollars a month for $g$ GB of data. What does the 5 mean?" options: ["5 dollars for each GB used", "5 GB of data are included", "The monthly fee is 5 dollars"] answer: 0 explain: "5 is m, the rate: each extra GB adds 5 dollars. The 20 is c, the fee you pay even with no data." ``` ### A phone plan Here is how to turn words into a rule. ```worked \text{Fee } 20, \text{ then } 5 \text{ per GB} :: A phone plan costs 20 dollars a month, plus 5 dollars for each GB used. Find a rule for the cost $T$. g = 0: \; T = 20 :: With no data used, you still pay the fee. That is the value when $g$ is 0. c = 20 :: The starting amount is $c$. m = 5 :: Each extra GB adds 5 dollars. "Per", "each" or "every" signals the rate, $m$. T = 5g + 20 :: Put them together. g = 3: \; T = 5(3) + 20 = 35 :: Check with a value you can work out in words: 3 GB costs 20 + 15 = 35 dollars. ``` ### Find the mistake Read Zoe's working one line at a time. How did she decide which number is $m$? ### What the numbers mean Read the rule back into words. ## Modify: new situations ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: no starting amount (c = 0), an amount that goes down (negative m), a rate that is not whole, and only two points with no words." try: { playground: board, starter: "graph.yml#no-fee", height: 640 } tasks: - starter: "graph.yml#no-fee" hint: "What does hiring the bike for 0 hours cost?" check: { type: board, text: "Bike hire: 6 dollars for 1 hour, 24 dollars for 4 hours. Set $m$ and $c$ so the line goes through both.", when: "P on y = mx + c and Q on y = mx + c", explain: "T = 6h: 6 dollars per hour and no fee, so c = 0 and the line starts at (0, 0)." } - starter: "graph.yml#down" hint: ["The battery goes from 80% to 50% in 3 hours. How much each hour?", "It goes down, so m is negative. Then work back to 0 hours for c."] check: { type: board, text: "A phone battery: 80% after 2 hours, 50% after 5 hours. Fit the line.", when: "P on y = mx + c and Q on y = mx + c", explain: "B = −10h + 100: it starts full (c = 100) and goes down 10% each hour (m = −10)." } - starter: "graph.yml#half" hint: "From 2 pages to 6 pages the cost goes up 2 dollars. How much per page?" check: { type: board, text: "Printing: 3 dollars for 2 pages, 5 dollars for 6 pages. Fit the line.", when: "P on y = mx + c and Q on y = mx + c", explain: "T = 0.5n + 2: a 2 dollar fee and 50 cents a page." } - starter: "graph.yml#points-only" hint: ["From 2 km to 4 km the fare goes up 6. How much per km?", "Work back from 2 km to 0 km to find the fee."] check: { type: board, text: "Two fares from a table: 11 dollars for 2 km and 17 dollars for 4 km. Find the rule.", when: "P on y = mx + c and Q on y = mx + c", explain: "T = 3d + 5: up 6 over 2 km is 3 per km, and 11 − 2 × 3 = 5 to get in." } ``` ### No starting amount Each task gives some values as points. (They are made up for the task.) Set $m$ and $c$ so the line goes through them all. ### Going down A phone battery runs down at the same rate each hour. ### Less than a dollar Printing costs a fee plus a little for each page. ### Only the numbers No words this time: just two fares. Work out the rate first. ## Practise: rules and meanings ```step stage: practise insight: "Writing a rule, reading its numbers in words and using it for a value are one skill; the review keeps solving with graphs fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Concert tickets cost 12 dollars each, plus a 6 dollar booking fee for the order. Write a rule for the total $T$ for $n$ tickets." answer: "12n + 6" feedback: - ["6n + 12", "Which amount is paid once for the whole order? That one is c."] - ["18n", "The booking fee is paid once, not for every ticket."] explain: "T = 12n + 6: 12 dollars for each ticket (m) and 6 dollars once (c)." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Try it with numbers first: what do 2 tickets cost in total, booking fee included, in dollars?", answer: 30, explain: "2 tickets at 12 dollars is 24, and the 6 dollar booking fee is paid once: 30." } - check: type: question q: "A plumber charges $T = 80h + 60$ dollars for a job of $h$ hours. What does the 60 mean?" options: ["A 60 dollar call-out fee, paid once", "60 dollars for each hour", "The cost of a 60-hour job"] answer: 0 explain: "60 is c: what you pay even for 0 hours, the call-out fee. 80 is the hourly rate." - check: type: answer q: "Using $T = 80h + 60$, what does a 3-hour job cost, in dollars?" answer: "300" feedback: - ["240", "That is the hours only (80 × 3). Add the call-out fee."] - ["420", "Check: 80 × 3 = 240, not 360."] explain: "80 × 3 + 60 = 240 + 60 = 300 dollars." - check: type: answer q: "Review: $y = 2x + 1$ and $y = 7$ meet at $(3, 7)$. Solve $2x + 1 = 7$." answer: "3" feedback: - ["7", "7 is the y of the meeting point. The solution is its x."] explain: "x = 3. Check: 2 × 3 + 1 = 7." ``` ### Tickets ### What the 60 means ### Using the rule ### Review ## Make: your own situation ```step stage: make insight: "Choosing a starting amount and a rate for a situation of their own reverses the lesson: from the rule back to words." try: { playground: board, starter: "graph.yml#make", height: 640 } hint: ["Pick a starting amount with c and a rate with m.", "Work out the total for 4 units: 4 lots of m, plus c. Drag P there."] check: { type: board, text: "Choose your own starting amount and rate (both more than 0). Then drag $P$ to the total for 4 units.", when: "P on y = mx + c and x(P) = 4 and m > 0 and c > 0", explain: "P is the total for 4 units: 4 lots of your rate, plus your starting amount." } ``` Invent a situation that is a starting amount plus a rate: a club with a joining fee and a weekly cost, a game with a starting score and points per level. Set $c$ and $m$, then drag $P$ to the total for 4 units. Stretch: tell a partner your situation in words. Can they write your rule? ## Make: a taxi trip on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Telling the one-off flag fall from the rate per km is the whole translation; the paper task makes them choose which number is c." hint: ["Which amount do you pay even for a trip of 0 km?", "Write the rule first, then put 14 in place of d."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A taxi company charges a flag fall of 5 dollars plus 3 dollars for each km (made up for the task). Write the rule for the fare $T$ for a trip of $d$ km, then work out the fare for a 14 km trip to the airport, in dollars." steps: - ["Flag fall 5 dollars, paid once: $c = 5$", "the amount for a trip of 0 km"] - ["3 dollars for each km: $m = 3$", "'for each' signals the rate"] - ["$T = 3d + 5$", "rate times distance, plus the flag fall"] - ["$T = 3 \\times 14 + 5 = 42 + 5$", "put 14 in place of $d$"] - ["The fare is $47$ dollars", "check: 14 km at 3 dollars is 42, and the flag fall makes 47"] picks: - step: 1 q: "Which number is c, the starting amount?" options: - "5 dollars, paid once to get in" - "3 dollars, because it comes second in the words" - "14, the length of the trip" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "3 dollars is paid again for every km. That is the rate, m.", "14 is the distance d, the input, not a starting amount."] answer: "47" feedback: - ["42", "That is the 14 km only (3 × 14). Add the 5 dollar flag fall."] - ["88", "Check: 5 + 3 = 8, then 8 × 14 would charge the flag fall every km. It is paid once."] criteria: - "I wrote c and m in words before the rule." - "My rule charges the flag fall once and the rate for each km." - "I put 14 in place of d and worked it out step by step." explain: "T = 3d + 5. For 14 km, 3 × 14 + 5 = 47 dollars." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. A real taxi's price card lists a flag fall and a rate per km, and the trip to the airport is a fare you can work out before you get in. Write c and m, then the rule, then type the fare. **Also used in** - **Taxi and ride-share fares.** A fare estimator is this rule with the rate and flag fall from the price card (waiting time and tolls are extras). - **Phone plans and gym memberships.** A fee paid once plus a rate for each GB or week is the same rule. - **Venue pricing.** A hire fee plus a price per guest has the same shape. ```teacher summary: Students turn a situation that is a starting amount plus a rate into a rule y = mx + c, read m and c back into words, and fit lines through real values (AC9M8A03, node 1). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can write a rule like T = 2d + 4 from a situation described in words. - I can explain what m and c mean in a situation (the rate and the starting amount). - I can use a rule to work out a value, and check it in words. struggle: Telling the one-off amount (c) from the rate (m) when the words give them in either order. Ask 'what would a trip of 0 km cost?' before they write the rule. before: > Do the Run and Modify boards yourself first. Students should already know what m and c do to a line (the first two lessons of this course). The new move is translation: the starting amount (paid once, the value when nothing has happened) is c; the rate ("per", "each", "every") is m. The order of the numbers in the words does not matter, and Zoe's working shows the mistake of assuming it does. The boards use the situation's own letters (T for total, d for distance), labelled on the axes. The graphs still behave exactly like y = mx + c. The next lesson uses these rules: two plans, where their lines cross, and when a rule stops being a good model. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. 'T = 4d + 2' is the common wrong answer: the numbers taken in the order they appear." - "Run: before students touch the sliders, ask: what would a 0 km trip cost? (4.) Where is that on the graph?" - "Investigate: model the worked example live. Underline 'a month' (once) and 'for each GB' (the rate) in the words, then write c and m." - "Modify: before the battery task, ask: which way will this line go?" - "Practise: for the plumber question, ask students to say what 80 means in words too." - "Make: pair students to swap situations and write each other's rules." - "Paper: the airport taxi task is worked in books; the page marks the fare (47) and that the flag fall of 5 is c. Books out, then look at the page for c and m named before the rule." stuck: - see: A student uses the numbers in the order they appear (Zoe's mistake). ask: Which amount is paid only once? Which is paid again for every km? fix: "Underline 'per', 'each' or 'every': that number is m. The one-off amount is c." - see: A student adds the fee into the rate (T = 6d). ask: What would a 0 km trip cost with your rule? With the real taxi? fix: "Work out 0 km and 1 km in words: 4 dollars and 6 dollars. The fee is paid once; only the 2 repeats." - see: A student cannot find c from two points (the last Modify task). ask: How much does the fare go up each km? What would 0 km cost? fix: "Work back from the first point one step at a time: 11 at 2 km, 8 at 1 km, 5 at 0 km." stretch: A candle is 20 cm tall and burns 1.5 cm an hour. Write its rule, and work out when it burns out. (h = 20 − 1.5t; after about 13.3 hours.) support: "Give a two-column table (0, 1, 2, 3 units) to fill in from the words before writing the rule: the 0 row gives c and the difference gives m." leads: > Next: comparing two plans. Two rules on one graph; where the lines cross is where they cost the same, and the model only makes sense for some values (no negative km). Where it leads in class: science graphs (a starting temperature and a heating rate), budgets and savings plans, and any "fee plus rate" price. exit: q: A swimming pool charges a 50 dollar membership plus 4 dollars a visit. Write the rule for the total T for v visits, and say what each number means. a: T = 4v + 50. 4 is the cost per visit (m); 50 is the membership, paid once (c). explain: > Many real amounts are a **starting amount plus a rate**. A taxi costs 4 dollars to get in, then 2 dollars for each km: $T = 2d + 4$. The starting amount is $c$: it is the value when nothing has happened yet (0 km), where the line crosses the axis. The rate is $m$: the words "per", "each" or "every" tell you it is the amount for each one more, how far the line goes up for each step. The order of the numbers in the words does not matter. Ask: which is paid once (c), and which is paid again and again (m)? ```

# Graph boards for "Rules from real situations". Each board shows some real values as points; students set m
# (the rate) and c (the starting amount) so the line goes through them all.

# region: run
widget: graph
axes: d (km), T ($)
x: -0.5, 6
y: -1, 18
slider m: 0, 4, 1
slider c: 0, 8, 0
plot: y = mx + c
point P: 1, 6
point Q: 3, 10
point R: 5, 14
# endregion

# region: no-fee
widget: graph
axes: h (hours), T ($)
x: -0.5, 6
y: -2, 36
grid: off
slider m: 0, 10, 2
slider c: 0, 10, 4
plot: y = mx + c
point P: 1, 6
point Q: 4, 24
# endregion

# region: down

axes: h (hours), B (%)
x: -0.5, 10
y: -5, 110
grid: off
slider m: -20, 20, 5, 5
slider c: 0, 120, 60, 10
plot: y = mx + c
point P: 2, 80
point Q: 5, 50
# endregion

# region: half

y: -1, 8

slider c: 0, 5, 0

point P: 2, 3
point Q: 6, 5

slider c: 0, 8, 0

# Zoe's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: zoe
A taxi costs 5 dollars to get in, plus 3 dollars per km.
m is the first number in the question, so m = 5.
c is the other number, so c = 3.
The rule is T = 5d + 3.
